event_description: By this date, Willawarrin is already receiving trucked water due to iron/manganese levels exceeding drinking water guidelines amid severe drought; Bellbrook is expected to need trucked water within a week. The Macleay River is near standstill and Steuart McIntyre Dam is at approximately 80% and falling. The exact date trucked water first began is not established by evidence yet - only that it predates this article's publication.
Willawarrin and Bellbrook are switched back to river water supply, ending several months of trucked-in water, following bore and treatment upgrades by Council's Water and Sewer team.

The water treatment infrastructure later replaced by the new 2025 plant is reported as having been built in 1967 (described elsewhere as "1960s-era"). The precise year rests on a single media report and has not been independently confirmed against a council asset record.

LC Water is reported as having been awarded the design-and-construction contract for the new Willawarrin plant, with an original cost projection of approximately $4 million. The exact contract-award date is not stated in the source; only the article's publication date (7 August 2024) is known.

NSW and Australian Governments announce a combined $52.9 million regional water infrastructure package, covering a new main treatment plant for Kempsey/Frederickton/Smithtown/Gladstone (Steuart McIntyre Dam/Sherwood Borefield) and reaffirming the separate $8 million Willawarrin plant commitment.
Construction begins (sod-turning) on the new $8 million Willawarrin water treatment plant - a 0.25 ML/day ultrafiltration plant with UV disinfection - with completion expected by early 2026.

Kempsey Shire Council moves to Level 2 water restrictions amid minimal forecast rainfall and declining Macleay River flow, naming Willawarrin and Bellbrook among the affected supply schemes. This is the earliest evidence found so far of the drought conditions behind the 2019-2020 trucked-water episode (CHR-0001), predating it by about five months.

The 2024 NSW Local Government election is held, contesting Kempsey Shire Council's mayoralty and councillor seats. EV-0011 (a Kempsey Shire Council-bylined item) states the results were 'for the September 9, 2024' election, but multiple independent sources place the statewide 2024 NSW Local Government polling day at Saturday 14 September 2024. Which date is correct for Kempsey specifically is not yet resolved (Q-0006).

The NSW Electoral Commission announces the preliminary distribution-of-preferences result for Kempsey Shire Council mayor: Kinne Ring elected with 53.67% after preferences, succeeding outgoing Mayor Leo Hauville.

The newly elected Kempsey Shire Council - Mayor Kinne Ring plus five new and three returning councillors - is formally sworn in (Oaths and Affirmations ceremony) at Council Chambers before the General Manager.

Kempsey Shire Council announces a $54 million water and sewer capital works program, naming Willawarrin as one of two new water treatment plant locations (with Crescent Head) - the earliest evidence found of the Willawarrin plant project, over two years before it reached tender stage.

Construction (sod-turning) begins on the Steuart McIntyre Dam/Sherwood Borefield plant - the larger $52.9m regional project distinct from the Willawarrin plant - consistent with EV-0005's announced mid-2025 start.
Bellbrook is gazetted, named for bellbirds along Nulla Nulla Creek.

Amid the Carrai East Bushfire (accelerating from 8 November 2019, during Kempsey's driest year on record), Bellbrook Public School becomes an impromptu evacuation centre, sheltering approximately 120 people plus pets and livestock, as the fire moves through the Bellbrook/Willawarrin area destroying homes and properties.

A Willawarrin resident is seen exiting his vehicle to open a gate providing access to Armidale Road, in the direction of the Willawarrin Hall evacuation point, during the Carrai East Bushfire; his body is found in nearby bushland on 13 November 2019. Recorded factually per coronial-inquiry reporting; no finding of fault or responsibility by any person or body is stated or implied.

A dedicated arsenic-removal water treatment plant is constructed at Bellbrook (approximate cost $700,000), addressing groundwater arsenic/heavy-metal contamination traced to historic Hillgrove-area mining.
Council begins carting water to Willawarrin, and intermittently to Bellbrook and the Thunggutti Aboriginal Community, during the bushfire/drought emergency.
Kempsey Shire Council moves to Level 3 water restrictions, up from the Level 2 restrictions in place since June 2019 (CHR-0007), showing continued escalation of the drought.

Water supply for parts of Kempsey and the Lower Macleay switches from the Sherwood Borefield to the Steuart McIntyre Dam, following continued dry weather and declining Macleay River flow - a drought-response event for the main network, distinct from the Willawarrin/Bellbrook-specific episodes.

Bellbrook's water treatment plant is taken offline due to persistent high manganese levels in source water, amplified by the drought event; water is carted from the Kempsey-Lower Macleay supply from this date until the plant returns to service on 18 June 2020 (CHR-0002).

Days after Bellbrook's plant returns to service, a Free Chlorine Critical Limit exceedance (4.1 mg/L against a 4.0 mg/L limit) occurs at the Clear Water Tank outlet, caused by elevated chlorine dosing needed to combat manganese carried over into the tank combined with low tank water levels; corrected within two days.

Willawarrin's raw-water turbidity exceeds its Critical Limit (3.12 NTU against a 2 NTU limit) following upriver rainfall; the plant is shut down and both bores isolated, with water carted from the Kempsey-Lower Macleay supply on 30-31 October and 2 November 2020 until the bores are flushed and the reservoir refilled by 3 November 2020.

Intermittent water carting from the Kempsey-Lower Macleay supply to Willawarrin (23 December 2020 to 11 January 2021) and Bellbrook (22 December 2020 to 7 January 2021), driven by wet-weather turbidity impacting source water.

Further water carting from the Kempsey-Lower Macleay supply: intermittently to Willawarrin (18 March to 13 April 2021) and continuously to Bellbrook from 21 March through to at least 30 June 2021 (the end of the reporting year covered by this source), driven by wet-weather and flood events.

Council's operational monitoring records four Manganese ADWG aesthetic exceedances at the Willawarrin reservoir outlet between this date and 14 December 2020 (0.18, 0.193, 0.2, and 0.159 mg/L, against the 0.1 mg/L aesthetic guideline) - the first actual measured contaminant concentrations obtained by this investigation for Willawarrin (THR-03/THR-04).

A Moderate to Major Flood Warning is issued for the Macleay River; Bellbrook's own river gauge reaches 10.55m, a major flood by its own classification (minor flood level 6.50m). Kempsey CBD floods after levees overtop; several Lower Macleay towns are isolated by road closures.
Bellbrook's raw (ground)water supply becomes contaminated by heavy metals and arsenic from former Hillgrove-area mines; elevated arsenic is detected in the town's drinking water through to 2007.

Water has to be trucked into Bellbrook because the town's water supply is too contaminated to use - a previously unknown, earlier trucked-water crisis, distinct from and predating the well-documented 2019-2020 episode by over a decade.

The Willi Willi Fire begins, eventually burning through the Kempsey Shire for several weeks - affecting 46% of the entire Shire, damaging or destroying 340 houses, outbuildings and fences, and directly impacting Willawarrin among other named localities. Formal disaster assistance is declared for the Kempsey LGA effective this date.

A dedicated bushfire recovery centre opens at Willawarrin Community Hall, run through 31 October 2023 with multiple state and community agencies present, supporting residents affected by the Willi Willi Fire.
